banner: All people and results here are fictional.
tagline: A private, kind guide to inherited health questions in families.
welcome.intro: KinSight explains screening results in plain words. It does not give medical advice and it never tells you what to decide.
result.title: My result
result.carrierNote: Being a carrier is not the same as having a condition.
couple.title: Couple view
couple.waiting: Waiting until both of you agree to share results for planning.
couple.tier3: A counsellor will review this with you.
couple.uncertainty: These figures are estimates and not a diagnosis. Being related can raise the chance for some conditions.
quiz.title: Check understanding
quiz.intro: Five short questions. There are no wrong answers to feel bad about; we simply explain again if something is unclear.
quiz.again: Let us explain this again in simpler words, then try once more.
quiz.done: Thank you. You understood the key points.
quiz.counsellorOffer: A counsellor can go through this with you. Would you like that?
consent.title: Consent centre
family.title: Family circle
family.hint: Relatives appear only as a relationship until they accept an invitation. Declining reveals nothing.
next.title: Next steps
next.intro: Options to talk through with a counsellor. They are listed in no order and carry equal weight. The choice is yours.
ask.title: Ask a question
ask.placeholder: Ask about your own result in plain words
ask.refusal: I can only help with your own result. I cannot share other people's information or tell you what to decide.
counsellor.title: Counsellor console
analyst.title: Analyst dashboard
analyst.suppressed: Counts below 10 are hidden and noise is added.
gov.title: Governance
gov.intended: Intended use: education and decision support for fictional cases. Not clinical advice.
limits: Limitations: synthetic data only, no real genomes, no clinical validation.
values.title: Questions to think about (for your own reflection or a counsellor chat)
values.q1: What matters most to you when thinking about this result?
values.q2: What would you like to know more about before talking with your partner or family?
values.q3: Who would you like to have with you when you talk with a counsellor?
voice.unsupported: Voice is not supported in this browser; please use text.

persona.desc.person_b: The other half of the couple
persona.desc.relative: A family member invited to see limited information

welcome.title: Understand inherited health risk, calmly and privately
result.lead: What was found for you, in plain words. Nothing is shared with anyone unless you choose.
couple.lead: The couple view appears only when both of you agree to share, and after a counsellor has reviewed it.
family.lead: Who is in your family circle and what each person may see.
consent.lead: Everything you share, with whom, why, and until when. Stop any of it with one tap.
next.lead: Things you can talk through with a counsellor. None is ahead of the others.
counsellor.lead: Cases assigned to you, with what you are allowed to see.
analyst.lead: Anonymous totals only. Small groups are hidden and noise is added to protect people.
gov.lead: How the system is checked: the audit trail, the rules, and where the data comes from.
ask.lead: Talk to Kin by typing or by voice, in English or Arabic. Kin only helps with your own result.
ask.empty: No questions yet. Try: What does my result mean?
welcome.asPerson: As a person or family member
brief.tier_3: Tier 3: a counsellor must review before release
brief.open: Open question: route to confirmatory assessment
policy.tier_priority_auto_tier1: Priority by tier, tier 1 handled automatically
settings.title: Comfort settings
palette.title: Search
palette.placeholder: Type a page, a term or a case
hero.sub: KinSight turns a screening result into plain words, shows what it means for a couple, and keeps a counsellor in the loop. It never tells anyone what to decide.
how.title: From result to the right next step
how.j1.d: The screening result arrives, per person.
how.j2.d: Plain words, pictures and a short check.
how.j4.d: Equal options, with owners and dates.
how.j5.d: Share only what you choose, with whom you choose.
punnett.caption: N is the usual copy of the gene, c is the changed copy. In each pregnancy: {aff} affected, {car} carrier.
journey.title: Your path
journey.note: Each step has an owner and a due date. Nothing closes without a recorded decision or evidence.
journey.expect.result_released: You have your result and explanation.
journey.expect.confirmatory_requested: A further test was asked for.
journey.expect.specialist_referral_reque: A specialist service was asked to see you.
couple.noFindings: No shared findings to show for this couple.
couple.relatedNote: Because you are related, the chance can be slightly higher than for unrelated couples.
next.o1.d: Talk with a genetic counsellor to go through the result.
next.o2.d: A further test can clarify a result.
next.o3.d: A specialist service can discuss the choices open to a couple.
next.o4.d: Support services can help families talk it through.
next.o5.d: There is no deadline to decide.
next.noSteps: No steps yet. They appear here once a counsellor or you record one.
learn.title: Learn the basics
learn.lead: Short, calm explanations. No jargon, no blame, no advice about what to decide.
learn.inherit.t: How a recessive condition is passed on
learn.inherit.d: When both parents carry one changed copy, each pregnancy can have one of three outcomes.
learn.inherit.note: A teaching example, not a result for any couple.
learn.chance.d: Pick an example to see it as people out of 100.
learn.chance.note: Examples only. A chance is an estimate, not a promise about any one child.
learn.myths: Common worries and what is true
summary.title: Take-home summary
summary.lead: One page to keep or bring to a counsellor visit.
summary.ask: Questions you may want to ask
summary.ask1: What does this result mean for us, in my own words?
summary.ask2: What further tests are possible and what do they involve?
summary.ask3: How certain is this estimate, and what could change it?
summary.ask4: Who else in the family might want to know, and how can I tell them?
summary.ask5: What support is available to us while we decide?
summary.choice: Every option here has equal weight. What you do next is your choice.
privacy.title: Privacy centre
privacy.lead: Who can see what, who has looked, and how to take control. The default is always no.
privacy.never: Nothing here is ever used for employment, insurance or commercial purposes. There is no download or export of personal data.
privacy.logNote: Every access and every refusal is recorded. Entries show who and why, never the content.
privacy.deleteWarn: This removes your results, relationships and agreements from this demo. The audit record keeps only that a deletion happened.
methods.title: Methods and evidence
methods.lead: How every number is made, how it is checked, and what has not been reviewed yet.
methods.kin: Kinship checks the engine must pass
methods.kinNote: Coefficient of a child whose parents are related as shown. Each value is a unit test.
methods.review: Review status: open. A genetics-trained reviewer and a native Arabic reviewer have not signed off yet (docs/REVIEWS.md).
methods.limits: These are standard textbook results on fictional data. They are not validated against a clinical source and must not be used for real decisions.
toolkit.title: Talking with family
toolkit.lead: Gentle ways to start the conversation. They never include the result itself.
toolkit.cardTitle: I would like to talk with you about a family health screening.
toolkit.cardBody: It is about looking after each other, not about blame. A counsellor can explain it in private if you would like.
toolkit.cardNote: This card contains no result and no names.
counsellor.sampleOnly: This is a sample queue entry. Only the demo case can be decided in this demo.
analyst.cohortNote: Based on {n} fictional couples; {r}% are related.
analyst.weeklyNote: Days from result to counsellor contact under first come, first served (illustrative simulation).
punnett.axes: Parent 1 is across the top and parent 2 down the side.
assistant.title: Kin, your assistant
assistant.name: Kin
assistant.intro: Ask about your own result in your own words, by typing or by voice. I reply in the language you use. I cannot talk about other people or tell you what to decide.
assistant.noMic: Voice input is not available in this browser. Please type instead.
assistant.micBlocked: The microphone is blocked. Allow it in the browser settings, or type instead.
assistant.noSpeechHeard: I did not hear anything. Try again, or type.
assistant.micError: Voice input did not work this time. Please type instead.
assistant.noVoice: This device has no {l} voice installed, so the reply is shown as text only.
assistant.noSpeech: Spoken replies are not available in this browser.
assistant.privacy: Kin runs in your browser, uses only your own consent-filtered information, never stores audio, and is not medical advice.
access.title: Finding services
access.lead: The kinds of service that can help at each step. All are listed with equal weight and in no order of preference.
access.disclaimer: KinSight names no clinic or hospital and cannot check what is available near you. A hand-off only records that you would like your screening service to contact you.
access.after: Your request is recorded in this demo only. In a real service, your screening service would contact you; this demo does not book appointments or promise availability.
access.confirmatory.d: A laboratory service that can run a further test to clarify a result.
access.confirmatory.w: Usually needs a referral from your counsellor or doctor.
access.counselling.d: Trained counsellors who explain results and answer questions without telling you what to do.
access.counselling.w: You can bring a partner or a family member if you wish.
access.primary.d: The service that arranged your screening and can answer practical questions.
access.primary.w: A good first contact if you are unsure where to start.
access.specialist.d: Specialists who can discuss the range of choices open to a couple.
access.specialist.w: Usually reached through a counsellor referral.
access.support.d: Support for families who want to talk through what a result means for them.
access.support.w: Open to relatives as well as to the couple.
